name: Work Holiday Pass (Work Holiday Programme)
summary: A 6-month pass for students and young graduates aged 18 to 25 whose university is in one of ten listed countries or regions. You apply yourself and do not need a job offer first.

requirements.text: You must be aged 18 to 25 when you apply.

sources.quote: You are aged 18 to 25 at the time of application.

requirements.text: Your university must be in Australia, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Netherlands, New Zealand, Switzerland, United Kingdom or United States, and recognised by that country's government.

sources.quote: You are an undergraduate or graduate of a university in Australia, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Netherlands, New Zealand, Switzerland, United Kingdom or United States.
Your university is recognised by the government of the respective ten countries or regions.

requirements.text: Graduates must have been a resident and a full-time student of that university. Undergraduates must have been so for at least 3 months before applying.

sources.quote: For undergraduates: you have been a resident and a full-time student of the university for at least 3 months before applying for the pass.
For graduates: you were a resident and a full-time student of the university.

requirements.text: The programme holds only 2,000 pass holders at any one time, so a place has to be free when you apply.

sources.quote: The Work Holiday Programme has a capacity of 2,000 pass holders at any one time.

requirements.text: The pass lets you stay and work in Singapore for up to 6 months.

sources.quote: Under the Work Holiday Programme, you can get a Work Holiday Pass that lets you stay and work in Singapore for up to 6 months .

requirements.text: If you will be working in a profession such as medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, architecture or law, you must also meet the registration requirements to practise in Singapore.

sources.quote: If you will be working in professions such as medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, architecture or law, you will need to comply with registration requirements to practise in Singapore.
